title: The Slow Descent

meta.veil: calls itself Progress; its true name, spoken in Urdu, is اترائی (subtitle: The Slow Descent). It stands for modernism.

scenes.title: The condition
scenes.where: The small mosque near the caves, just after Fajr.

items.speaker: SAIN
items.ur: تین دن میرے ساتھ چلو گے؟
items.en: Will you walk with me for three days?

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: کہاں؟
items.en: Where?

items.speaker: SAIN
items.ur: جہاں راستہ لے جائے۔ ایک شرط ہے: جب تک میں نہ بتاؤں، کیوں مت پوچھنا۔
items.en: Wherever the road goes. One condition: don't ask why until I tell you.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: منظور۔
items.en: Agreed.

clear: Sain asks for trust before he explains anything.
deep: Some knowledge only comes after patience. You can't argue your way to it.
deepest: This is the condition the hidden teacher sets in Surah Al-Kahf: "ask me about nothing until I mention it to you" (18:70). The next three acts follow that story with ordinary people.

scenes.title: The phone
scenes.where: A ridge path in the Margallas. Morning.
scenes.play: Walking. Burhan's phone keeps pinging with SURAT notifications.

items.text: Sain stops, holds out his hand, and Burhan gives him the phone. Sain smashes it on a rock.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: یہ کیا کیا آپ نے؟!
items.en: What did you just do?!

items.speaker: SAIN
items.ur: ابھی نہیں۔
items.en: Not yet.

clear: Something precious is broken for no reason Burhan can see.
deep: The phone is how the modern world goes everywhere with you.
deepest: In Al-Kahf, the boat is damaged to save it from a king who seized every sound boat. Its explanation comes in scene 12.

scenes.title: The chai stall
scenes.where: A roadside dhaba on the Murree road. Afternoon.
scenes.who: BURHAN, SAIN, an OLD MAN (a retired clerk).
scenes.play: The wheel opens, and Burhan's best proof line is lit and ready. Before the player can choose it, Sain's hand lands on his shoulder and the wheel closes.

items.speaker: OLD MAN
items.ur: نماز سے کیا ملتا ہے؟ میں نے چالیس سال نوکری کی، نماز کے بغیر۔ کیا بگڑا؟
items.en: What does prayer get you? I worked forty years without praying. What went wrong?

items.text: The wheel closes. Sain pays for the old man's tea and walks on. Burhan catches him up on the road.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: میں جیت رہا تھا!
items.en: I was winning!

items.speaker: SAIN
items.ur: ابھی نہیں۔
items.en: Not yet.

clear: Sain stopped Burhan from winning an argument.
deep: Winning an argument and winning a person are different things, and sometimes the first destroys the second.
deepest: The second act of the hidden teacher. Its meaning comes in scene 12.

scenes.title: The wall
scenes.where: Saidpur village at the foot of the Margallas. From evening through the night.
scenes.play: The villagers turn them away. Sain finds a crumbling old wall at the edge of one courtyard. All night, the player carries stones while Sain sets them in place.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: پانی مل سکتا ہے؟ ہم صبح سے چل رہے ہیں۔
items.en: Could we have some water? We've been walking since morning.

items.speaker: VILLAGER
items.ur: یہاں سیاحوں کو مفت کچھ نہیں ملتا۔
items.en: Tourists get nothing free here.

items.text: Sain is already lifting the first stone.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: ان لوگوں نے پانی تک نہیں دیا، اور آپ ان کی دیوار بنا رہے ہیں؟ کم از کم مزدوری تو مانگ لیں!
items.en: These people wouldn't even give us water, and you're building their wall? At least ask for wages!

items.speaker: SAIN
items.ur: ابھی نہیں۔
items.en: Not yet.

clear: Sain serves people who refused to serve him.
deep: Khidmat (service) that waits for a return is only trade.
deepest: In Al-Kahf, Musa says "if you wished, you could have taken a wage for it" (18:77). Here Burhan says the same thing.

scenes.title: The championship
scenes.where: A national TV studio. Faraz's network is broadcasting the National Debate Championship.
scenes.who: BURHAN REHAN (the opponent again) THE HOST, a young tech-optimist in a hoodie. In the real world he is just a man, but he wears Progress's mask. FARAZ, in the sponsor's box A live audience
scenes.play: The wheel opens as usual. Every option Burhan picks produces silence. His subtitle reads only (…). The crowd starts to murmur.

items.speaker: HOST
items.ur: آج کی قرارداد: یہ ایوان سمجھتا ہے کہ ترقی نے ہمیں بہتر انسان بنایا ہے۔
items.en: Tonight's motion: This house believes progress has made us better people.

items.speaker: REHAN
items.ur: ہم پہلے سے زیادہ جیتے ہیں، زیادہ جانتے ہیں، زیادہ آزاد ہیں۔ ترقی نے ہمیں بہتر بنایا ہے۔
items.en: We live longer, know more and are freer than ever. Progress has made us better.

items.text: The wheel opens and Burhan chooses. Nothing comes out. He tries again, and again there's nothing.

items.speaker: HOST
items.ur: ایک منٹ دیتے ہیں انہیں، فوکس۔ بیسٹ کو بھی کبھی کبھی اپ ڈیٹ چاہیے ہوتی ہے۔
items.en: Let's give him a minute, folks. Even the best need an update sometimes.

items.speaker: FARAZ
items.direction: from the box, under his breath
items.ur: چلو، چھوٹے...
items.en: Come on, little brother...

items.text: Burhan puts down the microphone and walks off the stage in silence.

clear: The champion debater loses his voice on the biggest night of his life.
deep: The lie "proof is enough" breaks in public. The motion itself is the Slow Descent's mask: longer, faster, more, and calling it better.
deepest: Imam Ghazali's tongue locked in front of his students in 1095. Burhan is about to meet him.

scenes.title: The escalators (the Gilding)
scenes.where: An endless golden mall of escalators that all go up, and up.
scenes.who: BURHAN (still voiceless), PROGRESS (a sleek figure in a hoodie whose screen face shows a loading bar stuck at 99%).
scenes.play: The reveal of the upgrade tree. The upgrades the player has been unlocking since chapter 1 (speed, influence, followers) light up one by one as escalator steps. Then a new gauge appears on the screen: TRUE ELEVATION: −1,240 m. They have been going down the whole time. Burhan tries to climb back, but the escalator outruns him and he falls.

items.speaker: PROGRESS
items.ur: اپ گریڈ کرو۔ تمہیں بہتر ہونے کا حق ہے۔
items.en: Upgrade. You deserve to be better.

items.speaker: PROGRESS
items.ur: ہر سال نیا ورژن۔ ہر سال تھوڑا اور اوپر۔
items.en: A new version every year. A little higher every year.

items.speaker: PROGRESS
items.ur: اوپر جانے کا احساس ہی تو اصل اوپر جانا ہے۔
items.en: The feeling of going up is what going up really is.

items.text: Burhan, exhausted and voiceless, sinks down on a step. Breath: Allah, Hu. The chain opens.

clear: Every upgrade felt like rising. They were sinking.
deep: "Progress" is not moral improvement, and convenience has a cost.
The game turns this critique on its own reward loop: the player's own upgrades were the staircase down.
deepest: "We will lead them on step by step, from where they do not know" (7:182). This is istidraj.

scenes.title: Baghdad, 1095 (vision)
scenes.where: The Nizamiyya college in Baghdad. A hall of three hundred students, then a bare room at night.
scenes.who: IMAM GHAZALI (featureless, in a scholar's turban, known by his silhouette and voice), STUDENTS, PHYSICIANS, BURHAN (voiceless).
scenes.play: Burhan watches the most famous teacher of his age fall silent, the way he just did. Burhan cannot speak. Ghazali speaks to him anyway.

items.text: In the hall, Ghazali opens his mouth to teach and nothing comes. The students whisper. Later, in a side room:

items.speaker: A PHYSICIAN
items.ur: بیماری جسم میں نہیں، دل میں ہے۔ دل کو فکر سے آرام ملے گا تو زبان کھلے گی۔
items.en: The illness isn't in the body; it's in the heart. When the heart finds rest from its worry, the tongue will open.

items.text: Night. Ghazali is folding a plain wool cloak. He sees Burhan at the door.

items.speaker: GHAZALI
items.ur: بولنے کی ضرورت نہیں۔ میں بھی چپ ہو گیا تھا۔
items.en: No need to speak. I fell silent too.

items.speaker: GHAZALI
items.ur: میں اس زمانے کا سب سے بڑا مدرس تھا۔ مگر جب اپنے دل میں جھانکا تو دیکھا: نیت اللہ کی نہیں، شہرت کی تھی۔
items.en: I was the greatest teacher of my age. But when I looked into my heart, I saw it: my intention was not for Allah, but for fame.

items.speaker: GHAZALI
items.ur: علم نے مجھے دروازے تک پہنچایا۔ اندر جانے کے لیے مجھے سب کچھ چھوڑنا پڑا۔
items.en: Knowledge brought me to the door. To go in, I had to leave everything.

items.text: He walks out through the city gate in the dark, carrying nothing.

clear: The greatest scholar of his age lost his voice, saw why, and walked away from fame.
deep: Knowing about God isn't knowing God, and learning done for prestige rots from inside.
deepest: Ghazali describes his locked tongue, the physicians' verdict and his departure in his own account, Deliverance from Error. His lines here are written for the game.

scenes.title: Cordoba (vision)
scenes.where: Cordoba in the 1190s: the courtyard of orange trees beside the great mosque, and a library with its doors open to the sun.
scenes.who: IBN RUSHD (a judge and philosopher, featureless, surrounded by books), BURHAN.

items.speaker: IBN RUSHD
items.ur: یہاں دلیل کی زبان کھلتی ہے۔ بولو۔
items.en: Here the tongue of reason opens. Speak.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.direction: his first words since the studio
items.ur: میرا نام... برہان ہے۔
items.en: My name... is Burhan.

items.speaker: IBN RUSHD
items.ur: دلیل۔ اچھا نام ہے۔
items.en: Proof. A good name.

items.speaker: IBN RUSHD
items.ur: حق، حق کا مخالف نہیں ہوتا؛ بلکہ اس کی موافقت کرتا اور اس کی گواہی دیتا ہے۔
items.en: Truth does not oppose truth; it agrees with it and bears witness to it.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: پھر مغرب نے دلیل کو دین سے الگ کیوں کر دیا؟
items.en: Then why did the West split reason from religion?

items.speaker: IBN RUSHD
items.ur: میں نے کہا تھا: حق، حق کا مخالف نہیں ہوتا۔ انہوں نے سنا: دو حق ہیں۔
items.en: I said: truth does not oppose truth. They heard: there are two truths.

items.text: He takes Burhan's hand and leads him through the library door into another century.

clear: A Muslim judge taught that reason and revelation agree.
deep: Reason was never the enemy of faith. Reason cut off from revelation is.
deepest: "Truth does not oppose truth" is Ibn Rushd's own principle, from Fasl al-Maqal ("The Decisive Treatise"). The word he used for demonstrative proof is burhan.

scenes.title: Paris, 1270s (vision)
scenes.where: A stone lecture hall in Paris, then a scribe's desk.
scenes.who: A MASTER lecturing in Latin. STUDENTS. A HERALD reading the bishop's condemnation of 1277. A SCRIBE. BURHAN and IBN RUSHD, unseen by the others.
scenes.play: Walking and watching. The people here are scholars at work, shown as they were. The scene is about what happened to an idea, not about the people.

items.speaker: MASTER
items.ur: Hoc verum est secundum philosophiam, sed non secundum fidem.
items.en: This is true according to philosophy, but not according to faith.

items.speaker: HERALD
items.ur: ...quasi sint duae contrariae veritates.
items.en: ...as if there were two contrary truths.

items.text: At the scribe's desk, a copy is being made. The name Ibn Rushd fades from the page and becomes Averroes. Another manuscript falls open at its first line: Dixit Algorizmi, "thus spoke al-Khwarizmi." The word algorithm lifts off the page and rises like gold leaf into a gold sky.

items.speaker: IBN RUSHD
items.ur: انہوں نے ہمارے نام لیے، اور ان سے وحی نکال دی۔
items.en: They took our names, and took the revelation out of them.

clear: Ideas born among Muslims went West and lost their roots on the way.
deep: Europe's "Averroists" were accused of teaching two truths, one for reason and one for faith. That was an early seed of the split that became secularism.
deepest: Burhan's name was stolen. The Gilding's code is written in a Muslim mathematician's Latinized name, algorithm, from Algorizmi.

scenes.title: Giving back (the Gilding)
scenes.play: The faqr mechanic. Prompt: Give back. Burhan returns his upgrades one by one: speed, influence, followers. Each one he gives up lifts the whole escalator. The true-elevation gauge climbs toward zero, then above it for the first time.

items.ur: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ أَنتُمُ الْفُقَرَاءُ إِلَى اللَّهِ
items.en: O mankind, you are the ones in need of Allah

items.speaker: PROGRESS
items.ur: رکو! تم پیچھے جا رہے ہو!
items.en: Stop! You're going backwards!

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: نہیں۔ پہلی بار اوپر جا رہا ہوں۔
items.en: No. For the first time, I'm going up.

items.text: Kashf. The loading bar cracks at 99%. Under the English mask PROGRESS, one Urdu word shows through: اترائی. Subtitle: THE SLOW DESCENT.

items.speaker: THE SLOW DESCENT
items.ur: میں نے تمہیں کبھی گرایا نہیں۔ بس ہر سیڑھی کو اوپر کا نام دیا۔
items.en: I never made you fall. I only called every step "up.

clear: Giving up the upgrades was the way up.
deep: Modern man feels self-sufficient, and the first revelation warned that man transgresses when he thinks himself self-sufficient (96:6–7).
deepest: Faqr is the station of knowing your need of Allah. It is the poverty that makes a person rich.

scenes.title: The bulldozers
scenes.where: Saidpur at dawn. Bulldozers stand at the edge of the old houses, under a banner: SAIDPUR HERITAGE RESORT — by Zar Developers.
scenes.who: BURHAN, SAIN, the VILLAGERS (the same ones who refused them water), the DEVELOPERS' MEN with sticks.
scenes.play: A fight. The villagers stand in front of their homes, and Burhan fights beside them, in control. The wall Sain built stands.

items.speaker: DEVELOPER'S MAN
items.ur: ہٹ جاؤ! یہ ترقی ہے! یہاں ریزورٹ بنے گا!
items.en: Move! This is progress! A resort's going up here!

items.text: The fight. The bulldozers pull back.

items.speaker: VILLAGER
items.ur: تم لوگ... ہمارے لیے لڑے؟ ہم نے تو تمہیں پانی تک نہیں دیا تھا۔
items.en: You people... fought for us? We didn't even give you water.

items.text: He goes inside and comes back with bread, water and a pot of saag.

clear: Burhan defends people who had refused him.
deep: "Progress" comes for the old village too, as a resort, as heritage turned into a product.
deepest: Service with no wage turns a hard heart. The villagers' food is the wage Burhan wanted in scene 4, and it came without asking.

scenes.title: Under the wall
scenes.who: BURHAN, SAIN. BILAL is sitting on top of the wall.
scenes.play: The explanations, in the order of Al-Kahf.

items.speaker: SAIN
items.ur: اب پوچھو۔
items.en: Now ask.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: میرا فون؟
items.en: My phone?

items.speaker: SAIN
items.ur: اس فون سے سُورت تمہیں دیکھ رہی تھی۔ تم جہاں جاتے، فراز کو پتا ہوتا۔
items.en: SURAT was watching you through that phone. Wherever you went, Faraz knew.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: وہ بوڑھا؟
items.en: The old man?

items.speaker: SAIN
items.ur: وہ کل فجر میں مسجد آنے والا تھا۔ اگر تم جیت جاتے، تو وہ ہار کر کبھی نہ آتا۔
items.en: He was going to come to Fajr tomorrow. If you had won, he'd have lost — and never come.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: اور یہ دیوار؟
items.en: And this wall?

items.speaker: SAIN
items.ur: یہ ایک یتیم کی ہے۔ اس کے باپ نے اس کے نیچے کچھ رکھا تھا۔ وقت آنے پر وہ خود نکالے گا۔
items.en: It belongs to an orphan. His father left something under it. When the time comes, he'll take it out himself.

items.text: Above them, Bilal swings his legs on the wall.

items.speaker: BILAL
items.ur: اوئے ہیرو! تم یہاں کیا کر رہے ہو؟
items.en: Oye, hero! What are you doing here?

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: تمہاری دیوار بنا رہے تھے۔
items.en: Building your wall.

items.speaker: BILAL
items.ur: میری دیوار؟
items.en: My wall?

clear: Each strange act had a reason Burhan couldn't see.
deep: We judge by what we can see, and the hidden is always larger.
deepest: The three explanations follow 18:79–82: the boat, the boy and the wall. The second is softened: here, what's saved is a man's return to prayer. "Their father was righteous" (18:82). The wall belongs to Bilal.

scenes.title: The professor
scenes.where: The village lane outside the wall. Night.
scenes.who: BURHAN, SAIN, BABA REHMAT (an old villager).

items.speaker: BABA REHMAT
items.ur: پروفیسر صاحب؟ آپ؟ تیس سال بعد؟
items.en: Professor sahib? You? After thirty years?

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: آپ... پروفیسر ہادی ہیں؟
items.en: You... are Professor Hadi?

items.speaker: SAIN
items.ur: تھا۔
items.en: I was.

items.speaker: BURHAN
items.ur: آپ نے سب کیوں چھوڑا؟
items.en: Why did you leave it all?

items.speaker: SAIN
items.ur: آج بغداد میں تم نے کیا دیکھا؟
items.en: What did you see in Baghdad today?

items.text: Burhan has no answer, and he doesn't need one.
اترائی — THE SLOW DESCENT. فقر — FAQR.
items.note: A third light glows above the first, on the left of Burhan's chest. This is the third latifa, sirr.

clear: The old sweeper was the legendary debater all along.
deep: He left the stage the way Ghazali left Baghdad. He is a malamati, hiding his worth under a broom.
deepest: The trophy in chapter 1 carried his name. Second-time players saw it coming. "Hadi" means guide.

notes: Al-Kahf. The three strange acts and their explanations follow the story of Musa and the hidden teacher (18:65–82), reframed with ordinary people. The second act is changed so that nothing is harmed. No prophet appears.
Ghazali's silence, the physicians' verdict and his departure are from his own al-Munqidh min al-Dalal.
"Truth does not oppose truth" is from Ibn Rushd's Fasl al-Maqal.
"As if there were two contrary truths" is from the Paris condemnation of 1277.
Dixit Algorizmi opens the Latin translation of al-Khwarizmi's arithmetic.
All other lines are written for the game.
The upgrade tree. It must exist from chapter 1, offering real, useful upgrades, or the twist has no weight.
To confirm with ulama: Ghazali and Ibn Rushd shown as featureless figures.
